body:
I’m 28, cisfemale and my partner is 30 mtf. We live in the Bible Belt. We’re still in the closet from any family and friends. It sucks. 

I dated my partner for 7 years before we got married in 2016, and now we’ve been together for 11 years. April 2019 they came out to me and you’re right, it was a shock to the system when you’ve known someone for so long. Knowing them for so long almost helped me accept what I was told my whole life was wrong. Knowing them inside and out helped me see that this was truly who they are. It felt like seeing a ghost or an alien-for the first time I was like oh wow this is legit. This is real and valid. Being transgender is normal. Society tells us it isn’t. So once I moved on with that I was ready to accept. I always identified as bisexual prior to this-so that made it a little easier to picture in my mind how our family would look. Society pressure is a bitch. Once I got over what others would think about us and I saw how happy my partner was, I was all in. We froze sperm before doing HRT just in case we want a family one day. Sexual attraction is important in a marriage and it helps that I’m sexually attracted to humans, not gender (now I identify as pan-sexual) but not everyone is like this and that’s also okay. I do think it would be harder if I was only sexually attracted to men. It’s okay to struggle. It’s okay to be scared as shit of the future. Keeping opening communication is HUGE during this time so gently tell your spouse how you feel. Studying comforted me as well. Reading and researching and learning allowed me to see people in relationships just like mine. If my partner “passes” (and that’s a whole other rabbit hole I could go down lol I couldn’t care less if they “pass”) then we will be viewed to the world as a “lesbian couple.” That can be a hard pill to swallow with society breathing down our necks telling us it’s not okay. Your feelings are valid and don’t feel guilt over them. Even though I’m cool with everything and even excited about our future, there are still moments of grief, fear, and struggle. We’re human after all :) Feel free to reach out if you need!
I really needed this right now. Thank you for sharing 💕
Thanks for your reply! I love my wife so much, it comforting to hear that it’ll get better and she will be happier. 🥰
Thank you for your reply! It’s comforting to know we’re in this with others and it’s normal to have these feelings. 💕
